fields.title: Two builds of kac are never compared

sections.What we are doing instead:
`dotnet run --project tooling/kac` builds from a checkout with the .NET SDK the repository pins, on a runner GitHub
gives fresh for every job. That is a reproducible environment by construction, and no standard here says so.

The package that reaches nuget.org is built once, by the publish workflow, from the commit on `main`. Nobody has ever built the same commit twice and compared the two `.nupkg` files.
sections.Why we need it: A byte-identical build needs `ContinuousIntegrationBuild`, a deterministic source path map and a source-link setup, and then a job that builds twice and diffs. That is real work against a threat this repository does not carry: the package is built by a workflow whose run is public, from a commit anybody can read.
sections.What compensates:
* The publish workflow is the only thing that builds what ships, and its run log names the commit.
* ctl-0007 stands a corpus up from the packed tool on every pull request, so what ships has been run.
* [tol-dotnet-sdk] pins the SDK, and [std-CONFIG] holds that pin to an exact version.
* nuget.org never lets a published version be replaced, so a rebuild cannot quietly overwrite what people already have.
sections.How it closes:
The publish workflow builds the package twice and fails where the two differ. A standard states the rule, and this record closes when both exist.

Where that is still not worth doing at the review date, the alternative is provenance: an attestation naming the workflow, the commit and the runner, which [dev-package-unscanned] also asks for.
sections.Scope: The `kac` package published to nuget.org, and the local builds a contributor runs.
